examples.en: The baby's breathing seems calm.
On winter mornings your breath looks white.
In the quiet room, only his breathing could be heard.
I felt a soft breath like a spring breeze.
She steadied her breath and began to sing.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 집에는 역사의 숨결이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The breath of history remains in this old house.

explain: '숨결'은 숨을 쉬는 모양이나 느낌이에요. 일상에서 숨 쉬는 것 자체는 '숨'이라고 하고, '숨결'은 글이나 노래에서 부드럽게 표현할 때 더 많이 써요. '역사의 숨결'처럼 어떤 분위기가 느껴진다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: I felt my mom's warm breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 가까운 느낌을 부드럽게 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to softly express the feeling of someone being close.

phrases.example: 이 오래된 집에서 역사의 숨결이 느껴져요.
phrases.en: I can feel the breath of history in this old house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 분위기나 시간이 가까이 있는 것 같다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you sense an atmosphere or era as if it were close.

phrases.en: I can feel the breath of spring in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이 오는 느낌을 글이나 노래처럼 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A poetic way to describe the feeling of a season arriving.

explain_en: 숨결 is how breathing looks or feels. Everyday breathing itself is just 숨, while 숨결 is used more in writing and songs for a soft feeling. It can also mean a sense of atmosphere, as in 역사의 숨결.

examples.en: Silver hair suits my grandmother so nicely.

examples.ko: 은발의 신사가 지하철에서 자리를 양보해 줬어요.
examples.en: A silver-haired gentleman gave me his seat on the subway.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 머리를 은발로 염색해서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That actor dyed his hair silver and became a hot topic.
Before I knew it, my father's hair had turned silver.

examples.ko: 은발 머리를 길게 묶은 할아버지가 지나갔어요.
examples.en: An old man with long silver hair tied back walked by.

examples.ko: 은발이 잘 어울리는 사람은 생각보다 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many people look good in silver hair.

explain: 흰머리를 멋있고 곱게 말하고 싶을 때 '은발'을 써요. 그냥 나이 들어 센 머리는 '흰머리'라고 하고, '백발'도 비슷하게 써요. 젊은 사람이 일부러 염색한 머리에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My father has more gray hair these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 들어 센 머리를 말하는 가장 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest word for hair that has turned white with age.

phrases.en: My grandfather's hair has turned white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완전히 하얗게 센 머리예요. '은발'보다 멋을 담지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Completely white hair; it doesn't carry the elegant feel of 은발.

phrases.en: My friend dyed her hair silver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 사람이 멋으로 하는 머리에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also describe a stylish look chosen by young people.

explain_en: Use '은발' when you want to describe white or grey hair in a nice, elegant way. Plain aged hair is usually called '흰머리', and '백발' is similar. It can also be used for hair that a young person dyed silver on purpose.

examples.en: My younger sibling talked in their sleep last night and startled me.
My husband sometimes talks loudly in his sleep.
I have a habit of talking in my sleep when tired.
That friend talked in his sleep at camp last night.

examples.ko: 잠꼬대할 때 무슨 말을 하는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I am curious what I say when I talk in my sleep.
It was cute to see the child talking in her sleep while smiling.

explain: '잠꼬대'는 명사이고 '잠꼬대하다'가 그 행동이에요. 깨어 있을 때 앞뒤가 안 맞는 말을 하면 '잠꼬대 같은 소리'라고 놀리듯 말해요. 이때는 '무슨 잠꼬대야?'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 지금 무슨 잠꼬대 같은 소리를 하는 거예요?
phrases.en: nonsense talk
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨어 있는데도 말이 앞뒤가 안 맞거나 엉뚱할 때 핀잔주듯이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to scold or tease someone who is talking nonsense while awake.

explain_en: 잠꼬대 is the noun, and 잠꼬대하다 is the action. When someone talks nonsense while awake, Koreans tease with 잠꼬대 같은 소리. You can also say 무슨 잠꼬대야? in that case.

examples.en: I get scared just by looking at an injection needle.
It stings when the needle goes into my arm.

examples.ko: 새 주삿바늘은 한 번만 쓰고 버려요.
examples.en: A new needle is used once and thrown away.
The child burst into tears because of the needle.
The nurse carefully took out the needle.
Be careful not to get pricked by the needle.

explain: '주사'와 '바늘' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가서 '주삿바늘'이라고 써요. 주사를 맞을 때 몸에 들어가는 가는 바늘 부분을 말해요.

phrases.en: The nurse got hurt by a syringe needle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바늘에 실수로 찔렸을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is pricked by a needle by accident.
phrases.en_equiv: get pricked by a syringe needle

phrases.en: After the injection, they removed the needle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주사가 끝나고 몸에서 바늘을 뺄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking the needle out after an injection.

phrases.en: Hospitals use a new syringe needle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위생을 말할 때 '새 주삿바늘'이라고 자주 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about hygiene.

explain_en: A linking 'ㅅ' (사이시옷) is added between '주사' and '바늘', so it is written '주삿바늘'. It refers to the thin needle part that goes into the body during an injection.

examples.ko: 봄만 되면 춘곤증 때문에 낮에 졸려요.
examples.en: Every spring I get sleepy during the day because of spring fatigue.

examples.ko: 춘곤증이 와서 오후 내내 하품이 나요.
examples.en: Spring fatigue has hit me, and I yawn all afternoon.
They say light exercise is good for beating spring fatigue.
They say spring fatigue gradually gets better as the weather warms up.
I keep feeling tired lately, maybe because of spring fatigue.

examples.ko: 저는 춘곤증에 커피보다 산책이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For spring fatigue, a walk helps me more than coffee.

explain: 봄이 되면 나른하고 졸린 느낌이 드는 증상이에요. 봄 날씨 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. 점심 먹은 뒤에 졸린 것은 '식곤증'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I have spring fatigue these days, so I'm always sleepy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증상이 시작될 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural phrase for when the symptoms start.

phrases.en: I got over my spring fatigue with a cup of coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸음을 참거나 극복할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you fight off or overcome the sleepiness.

phrases.en: I dozed off in class because of spring fatigue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원인을 말할 때 붙이는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give the cause of something.

explain_en: It's the sluggish, sleepy feeling people get when spring arrives, and it comes up often in talk about spring weather. The sleepiness after lunch is called '식곤증'.

examples.en: I've been coughing all day because of my cold.
If you keep coughing, please go see a doctor.
The person next to me kept coughing, so I was worried.
Why are you coughing so much since this morning?
I could hear the child coughing all night.
Many people are wearing masks and coughing.

explain: '기침하다'는 그냥 기침을 한다는 말이고, '콜록거리다'는 기침 소리가 계속 나는 모습을 생생하게 말할 때 써요. 주로 감기에 걸렸을 때 들어요. '콜록거리다' 말고 '콜록콜록하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I coughed all night and couldn't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '콜록거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 소리를 흉내 낸 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 콜록거리다, using the cough-sound word.

phrases.en: He came into the meeting coughing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기침하는 동작과 다른 행동을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say another action happens while coughing.

phrases.en: I cough when I breathe in cold air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기침을 한다는 일반적인 말이고, 소리 느낌은 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The general word for coughing, without the sound imagery.

explain_en: '기침하다' simply says someone coughs, while '콜록거리다' vividly describes the sound of repeated coughing. It is mostly used when someone has a cold. People also say '콜록콜록하다'.

examples.en: The man grew a stylish mustache.

examples.ko: 아빠가 콧수염을 깎고 나니 젊어 보여요.
examples.en: Dad looks younger after shaving off his mustache.
The grandfather with a mustache is smiling.
The villain in the cartoon has a long mustache.
A mustache has to be trimmed every morning.
I got a milk mustache after drinking milk.

explain: 코 아래에 난 수염이에요. 턱에 난 수염은 '턱수염', 뺨 쪽은 '구레나룻'이라고 불러서 위치마다 이름이 달라요. '코'에 'ㅅ'이 붙어 '콧'이 되는 소리 변화도 눈여겨보세요.

phrases.en: My son has started to grow a mustache.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수염이 자라기 시작할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when facial hair starts to grow.

phrases.en: I trim my mustache in front of the mirror.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 정리할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for tidying up the shape.

phrases.en: Grandpa grows a beard too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콧수염과 위치가 달라서 같이 비교해 알아 두면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A different location than the mustache, useful to learn together.

explain_en: Hair growing under the nose. Chin hair is 턱수염 and sideburns are 구레나룻, so each place has its own name. Note the sound change where 코 gets an added ㅅ to become 콧.

examples.en: The baby's cheeks have filled out chubbily.

examples.ko: 강아지가 밥을 잘 먹어서 포동포동 살쪘어요.
examples.en: The puppy eats well and has gotten plump.
I met a cute child with chubby little hands.

examples.ko: 고양이 발이 포동포동해서 자꾸 만지고 싶어요.
examples.en: The cat's paws are so chubby that I keep wanting to touch them.

examples.ko: 포동포동 살이 오른 팔뚝이 정말 귀여워요.
examples.en: Those plump little arms are really adorable.

examples.ko: 병원에서 아기가 포동포동 잘 크고 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: At the clinic, they said the baby is growing nicely and plump.

explain: 아기나 작은 동물처럼 살이 보드랍게 올라 귀엽게 통통한 모습이에요. 어른에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니, 주로 아기, 강아지, 고양이에게 써요. '통통'보다 더 부드럽고 귀여운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The baby's hands are chubby and cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사가 아니라 '하다'를 붙여 모습을 설명하는 형용사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 makes it an adjective that describes appearance.

phrases.en: I want to touch those chubby cheeks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: The baby got chubby after eating baby food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살이 올라 변하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the change of becoming plump.

explain_en: It describes soft, cute plumpness, as on babies and small animals. Using it for adults can be rude, so it is mostly for babies, puppies and kittens. It feels softer and cuter than '통통'.

en: to clear one's throat; to hem

examples.en: Grandfather cleared his throat in front of the door and came in.

examples.ko: 말을 꺼내기 어려워서 몇 번 헛기침했어요.
examples.en: It was hard to bring it up, so I cleared my throat a few times.
When I'm embarrassed, I clear my throat without realizing it.
Why do you keep clearing your throat?
Someone in the back row cleared their throat on purpose.
He cleared his throat and changed the subject.

explain: '기침하다'는 몸이 아파서 하는 기침이고, '헛기침하다'는 신호를 보내거나 어색함을 감추려고 일부러 하는 기침이에요. 명사 '헛기침'과 같이 '헛기침을 하다'로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: He felt awkward and cleared his throat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '헛기침'과 '하다'를 띄어 써도 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Writing the noun and 하다 separately means the same.

phrases.en: He came into the room clearing his throat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면서'로 두 동작을 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -(으)면서 joins two actions done together.

phrases.en: I heard someone clearing their throat at the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 명사 앞에서 '-는'으로 바꾼 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb changed to -는 before a noun.
phrases.en_equiv: the sound of clearing one's throat

explain_en: '기침하다' is coughing because of illness, while '헛기침하다' is a deliberate cough to send a signal or hide awkwardness. People also say '헛기침을 하다' with the noun.

examples.ko: 휴가 때 햇볕에 타서 피부가 구릿빛이 됐어요.
examples.en: I got tanned in the sun on vacation and my skin turned bronze.
Bronzed skin looks healthy.
That athlete's bronzed forearms look great.
I walked through the autumn fields tinted copper.
The old statue has a copper hue.
I saw a bronze-skinned surfer on the beach.

explain: 구리처럼 붉은 갈색을 띠는 색이에요. 햇볕에 보기 좋게 탄 피부를 말할 때 가장 자주 나오고, 보통 건강하고 멋진 느낌이에요. 사이시옷 때문에 '구리삗'으로 소리 나요.

phrases.en: A man with a sun-tanned face is smiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구릿빛 피부'보다 얼굴만 콕 집어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you mean just the face, rather than skin in general.

phrases.example: 여름 내내 바닷가에서 놀아서 구릿빛으로 탔어요.
phrases.en: I played at the beach all summer and got a bronze tan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구릿빛이 되다'보다 햇볕에 타는 과정을 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This focuses on the process of getting tanned in the sun.

phrases.en: The athlete's bronzed arms look strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔, 다리처럼 몸의 한 부분에도 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can attach it to body parts like arms and legs.

explain_en: It is the reddish brown of copper. It most often describes skin nicely tanned by the sun, usually with a healthy, attractive feel. Because of the 사이시옷, it is pronounced '구리삗'.

examples.en: I divided the dough into lumps and baked them.
I packed the snow into one lump.
I put a chunk of meat in the fridge.
I made a doll out of a lump of clay.
I broke the lump of soil with my hands.
The rice clumped together and tastes bad.

explain: '덩이'는 혼자 쓰기보다 '고깃덩이', '눈덩이', '흙덩이'처럼 다른 말 뒤에 붙는 경우가 많아요. 또 '한 덩이, 두 덩이'처럼 덩어리를 세는 단위로 써요. 비슷한 '덩어리'가 일상에서 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: I put the lump of meat into the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '덩이'를 다른 말 뒤에 붙인 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound word with 덩이 attached to another word.

phrases.en: I broke the clod of soil with my hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흙이 뭉친 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for soil stuck together in a lump.

phrases.en: The sugar clumped into lumps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '덩이'보다 '덩어리'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 덩어리 is more common than 덩이.

explain_en: '덩이' is more often attached to another word, as in '고깃덩이', '눈덩이' and '흙덩이', than used alone. It is also a counter for lumps, as in '한 덩이, 두 덩이'. The similar '덩어리' is more common in daily speech.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 뺨이 불그스레해요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, so my cheeks are slightly red.
The sky was tinged red by the sunset.
The thin, reddish lips were striking.
Maybe from embarrassment, that kid's face turned slightly red.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려 코끝이 불그스레하고 열이 나요.
examples.en: I caught a cold, so the tip of my nose is reddish and I have a fever.

examples.ko: 색은 불그스레하지만 맛은 별로 달지 않은 사과예요.
examples.en: It's an apple that looks reddish but is not very sweet.

explain: '빨갛다'보다 연하고 은은하게 붉은 느낌이라 얼굴, 뺨, 노을처럼 살짝 붉을 때 어울려요. 같은 뜻으로 '불그스름하다'도 쓰지만, 활용할 때는 '불그스레해요'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The apple skin is slightly red.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불그스레하다'와 뜻이 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 불그스레하다.

phrases.example: 술을 마셔서 얼굴이 불그스레한 사람이 많았어요.
phrases.en: Many people had flushed faces from drinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '불그스레한'으로 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it becomes 불그스레한.

phrases.example: 저녁 햇빛 때문에 벽이 불그스레해 보여요.
phrases.en: The wall looks reddish because of the evening sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something looks that way.

explain_en: It is softer than '빨갛다' and suggests a faint redness, suitable for faces, cheeks, and sunsets. '불그스름하다' means about the same. The conjugation is '불그스레해요'.

examples.en: The apples ripened bright red in the autumn sun.
I was so embarrassed that my face turned bright red.

examples.ko: 새빨간 장미 한 송이를 선물로 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a single deep red rose as a gift.
My nose is bright red from the cold weather.
The sunset dyed the sky bright red.
I cried all night, so my eyes are swollen and bright red.

explain: '빨갛다' 앞에 '새-'가 붙어서 아주 짙고 선명한 빨강을 말해요. ㅎ불규칙이라서 '새빨개요', '새빨간', '새빨갛게'로 바뀌어요. 같은 계열의 '시뻘겋다'는 더 크고 거센 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 그 사람 말은 모두 새빨간 거짓말이었어요.
phrases.en: Everything that person said was a total lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금도 사실이 아닌 뻔한 거짓말을 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress a lie that has no truth in it at all.

explain_en: Adding '새-' to '빨갛다' gives a very deep, vivid red. It is a ㅎ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '새빨개요', '새빨간' and '새빨갛게'. The related '시뻘겋다' feels bigger and heavier.

en: to be widely known; to be widely spread

examples.en: That restaurant is the talk of the town for its taste.

examples.ko: 그 선생님에 대한 칭찬이 학교에 자자했어요.
examples.en: Praise for that teacher was all over the school.

examples.ko: 소문이 자자하던 가게에 드디어 가 봤어요.
examples.en: I finally visited the shop everyone had been talking about.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 헤어졌다는 소문이 자자한데 사실일까요?
examples.en: There's talk everywhere that the two broke up, but is it true?
They say that actor's popularity is huge overseas too.

examples.ko: 칭찬이 자자하면 누구나 한 번 가 보고 싶어져요.
examples.en: When the praise is everywhere, anyone wants to go once.

explain: '자자하다'는 '소문이 자자하다', '칭찬이 자자하다', '명성이 자자하다'처럼 소문, 평판과 관련된 말과만 붙어요. 좋은 소문에도 나쁜 소문에도 쓰지만 실제로는 칭찬이나 인기에 가장 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I went to a bakery with a great reputation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form that describes a noun after it.

phrases.en: Everyone is praising that student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 입을 모아 칭찬한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many people are praising someone.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 노래 실력으로 명성이 자자했어요.
phrases.en: That singer was widely famous for his singing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름이나 평판이 널리 알려졌다는 뜻으로, 과거의 일은 '자자했어요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a name or reputation is widely known; use 자자했어요 for the past.

explain_en: '자자하다' only pairs with words about rumor or reputation, such as '소문이 자자하다', '칭찬이 자자하다' and '명성이 자자하다'. It works for both good and bad talk, but in practice it is used most for praise and popularity.

examples.ko: 우리 집 꼬맹이가 벌써 학교에 가요.
examples.en: The little one in our house already goes to school.
I am amazed that little kid has grown this big.
Little kids are running around in the park.

examples.ko: 꼬맹이 때 사진을 보면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: I laugh when I see photos from when I was a little kid.
I gave some snacks to the little kid next door.
Our youngest is still just a little kid.

explain: 꼬맹이는 작은 아이를 귀엽게, 조금 장난스럽게 부르는 말이에요. 친구나 가족끼리 편하게 쓰고, 어른에게나 공식적인 자리에서는 '어린이', '아이'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '꼬마'도 있어요.

phrases.en: That little kid is my younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼬맹이와 비슷하지만 조금 덜 장난스럽고 더 널리 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 꼬맹이 but a little less playful and used more widely.

phrases.example: 제가 꼬맹이 때는 이 동네가 아주 작았어요.
phrases.en: When I was a little kid, this neighborhood was very small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렸을 때를 편하게, 귀엽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, affectionate way to say 'when I was little'.
phrases.en_equiv: when I was a little kid

phrases.en: The little kids are playing in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 아이를 귀엽게 함께 부를 때 '들'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 들 to affectionately refer to several small kids together.

explain_en: Kkomaengi is an affectionate, slightly playful name for a small child. Friends and family use it casually; in formal settings people say 어린이 or 아이 instead. 꼬마 is a similar word.
